context: Algebraic construction of Z as the additive group completion of N
formulation: Define an equivalence relation on N×N by (a,b)∼(c,d) precisely when a+d=b+c. The integers can be constructed as equivalence classes Z=(N×N)/∼, with [a,b] representing the formal difference a−b.
reason: ProofWiki formally constructs integers as the inverse completion of natural numbers. This equivalence relation is independent of rational numbers and gives explicit representatives without assuming integer subtraction already exists. The induced addition and multiplication require separate well-definedness checks, so this is an independently described construction, not a proof the resulting quotient is an integral domain.
caveats: Do not define (a,b) equivalence using subtraction of integers before Z is constructed.
The additive inverse and multiplication need independent verification.
Natural number model/order convention may vary; keep N domain explicit.

context: Commutative unital integral domain Z under integer addition and multiplication
formulation: The ring of integers is the algebraic structure (Z,+,·), where Z is the set of integers, + is integer addition, and · is integer multiplication. It is a commutative ring with identity 1 and no zero divisors.
reason: The dedicated ProofWiki ring-of-integers definition introduces the integer ring and directs readers to theorems that verify its ring and integral-domain properties. The structural assertion that (Z,+,·) is an integral domain is a theorem/property, not itself the definition of integer ring; it must remain distinguishable in publication from the bare named structure.
caveats: Do not conflate with ring of integers of an algebraic number field.
Integral-domain status must be separately justified rather than assumed from a bare ring name.

term: fraction field of an integral domain
context: Equivalence-class fractions and universal property of an integral-domain fraction field
formulation: For a commutative integral domain D, its fraction field Frac(D) can be constructed from pairs (a,b) with a∈D and b∈D\{0}, identifying (a,b) with (c,d) when ad=bc. The class of (a,b) is denoted a/b. Addition and multiplication of these classes yield a field into which D embeds as a subring.
reason: Stacks Project Example 9.3.4 gives explicit fraction equivalence and the universal property; ProofWiki gives an independently checked field-of-quotients formulation involving an injective embedding into a field. The construction requires D to be an integral domain to support the equivalence criterion and well-defined inverses of nonzero classes. Q is the instance D=Z; general fraction fields and total quotient rings for rings with zero divisors are not the same context.
caveats: Do not silently merge total quotient rings of rings with zero divisors with fields of fractions.
Distinguish a concrete pairs quotient from an abstract universal-property characterization.
Proof of field laws and universal property is a separate theorem.
